(4) 300 sequential and then 120 concurrent reads of keys no issue carries all answer 404, a live issue still reads afterwards, and the shared pool holds 0 connections with 863 returned. (5) 160 concurrent reads across the issue read, the artifact list, the ask list and the event page all answer the bytes each route answers alone. (6) Each of those three routes now sends exactly one detail batch: /artifacts 2 round trips (1 batch of 3), /asks?state=all 2 (1 batch of 2), /events 3 (1 batch of 2).

proof.criterion: (c) The change is not slower on the routes it changes
proof.surface: The real envoy-dispatch binary over a real socket, same database and same 228-issue corpus, measured by the Dispatch process's own utime+stime from /proc/<pid>/stat across the window. The mix is the issue read, the issue artifact list, the issue ask list, the issue event page and the two project artifact lists - every route this round moved.
proof.command: python3 load2.py keys.json <side>-<n> 45 8 0 - eight closed-loop clients for 45 s, each run preceded by a discarded 5 s warm-up and by a restart of the binary under test on the unchanged database, base and head alternating over three pairs
proof.observed: Every head run is cheaper than every base run on every measure. CPU per request: base 1.496, 1.525, 1.508 ms; head 0.852, 0.861, 0.918 ms. Throughput: base 324.7, 328.6, 324.8 rps; head 543.3, 523.7, 513.9 rps. Dispatch CPU over the 45 s window: base 21.90, 22.61, 22.10 s; head 20.84, 20.31, 21.23 s, at 1.6x the requests. p95: base 77.7, 74.5, 79.5 ms; head 34.7, 36.9, 37.6 ms. p99: base 353.2, 343.8, 348.3 ms; head 55.4, 67.0, 63.4 ms. Every request of all six runs answered 200 (14,640 to 24,462 per run). Head's p50 is higher (11.2-11.5 ms against 9.7-9.8), which is what a closed-loop load shows when throughput rises: the eight clients are kept busier, and p95, p99 and cost per request all fall.
proof.negativeControl: Base and head were each measured three times, alternating, each from its own restart: the base spread is 0.029 ms per request (1.496 to 1.525) and the head spread 0.066 ms (0.852 to 0.918), both far below the 0.6 ms gap between the sides, so the ordering is not run-to-run noise.

proof.surface: The same stack and corpus, with a fifth of the reads asking for keys no issue carries, so every one of those reads closes a batch that used to return an error. Three binaries: base 5dc21cb9, head 411260c2, and a mutant of head with the issue-row callback returning pgx.ErrNoRows into Close again, which is exactly the code the review asked to be changed.
proof.command: python3 load2.py keys.json <side>-<n> 45 8 0.2, two rounds of the three binaries, each from its own restart with a discarded 5 s warm-up
proof.observed: head 465.2 and 488.8 rps at 0.770 and 0.735 ms CPU per request, p50 14.1/13.8 ms, p95 38.6/36.8, p99 73.5/62.0. The mutant 356.8 and 354.5 rps, p50 18.4/18.7 ms, p95 52.9/53.5, p99 87.5/82.5 - 24% less throughput than head on the same load, with Dispatch's own CPU *lower* (13.19 and 13.13 s against head's 16.13 and 16.18), because the cost of re-preparing the batch's statements is Postgres's and the server simply gets less done. Base 390.0 and 396.8 rps at 1.274 and 1.313 ms CPU per request, p99 342.1 and 342.8 ms. So the finding was real and the fix earns its place: the head is faster than base and faster than the head that keeps the old return.

reviewFindingsCheckedOnTheSurface: Finding 1 (statement cache): verified twice - the implementer's test passes at head and fails with the return put back, and under a 20% missing-key load the mutant does 24% less work than head (proof entries 'missing-key cost' and 'round trips').

Finding 2 (dead loaders): loadOpenAsks and loadChildren are gone from issue_queries.go; the issue read, the ask list and the event page all still answer base's bytes, which is the behaviour those loaders carried.

Finding 3 and 4 (one queue-and-apply per lookup, one export each): the five routes that now share it - loadArtifacts, listProjectArtifacts, queryOwnerAsks, the Inbox and the event page - are all in the 2,708-target comparison and all answer base's bytes, and the three that carry details measure exactly one detail batch each.
Finding 5 (one response type): issueDetail is the response getIssue writes; the byte comparison covers it.

Finding 6 (the round-trip count and the strip sample): the count now takes only the counted request's statements (countedRead in the request context), and the strip sample fails under writtenTree(node, true), which closes the limit I recorded in round 2.

The implementer's documented errorTextDifference - a failure that is not a statement's own now surfaces from SendBatch(...).Close() without attachApprovals' loader prefix - is not user-visible: the handler answers {"code":"INTERNAL","error":"internal server error"} for any such failure, as the identity-event probe shows, and the prefix only ever reached the log.
